extracted.intended_audience: literary scholars, critics, and serious writers interested in Coleridge and the craft/ethics of literary prose
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for producing serious literary writing and criticism that is intellectually honest, stylistically illuminating, and not degraded by partisan, commercial, or purely popular aims. Emphasizes balance between contemplative freedom and disciplined practice, historical/philosophical accuracy, and clarity when treating spiritual or metaphysical topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make important truths accessible in language
rubrics_metrics.description: Clothe important truths 'in such language as renders their reception more easy to minds not entirely petrified by the materialism of the day.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, receptive phrasing so profound ideas are intelligible to readers influenced by contemporary materialism; style should aid understanding rather than obscure substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid adapting serious writing to vulgar periodical styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not 'adapt it to the ways of the newspapers' or descend into 'vulgar periodical writing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist pressure to conform serious prose to the norms or quick-tempo demands of popular periodicals; preserve depth and seriousness rather than pandering to ephemeral journalistic fashions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize higher aims over literary commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline to make literature merely 'the means of living' if that entails debasing it; avoid sacrificing 'higher aims for the sake of immediate popularity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value intellectual and moral purposes of writing above short-term financial or popular success; accept narrower livelihood rather than reducing literary standards to commercial expediency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue literature as intellectual discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature, liberally pursued, disciplines the mind by abstraction and reflection and 'better disciplines that life which consists in seeking the things that are above.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate contemplative and reflective habits via literary study/writing; treat literature as formative of thought and character rather than mere entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid long engagement in inferior pursuits that dull higher faculties
rubrics_metrics.description: Inferior pursuits may sooner weary and disgust, and during continuance they more unfit the mind for higher ones; do not let one set of lower engagements leave the soul unfit for higher receptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of prolonged involvement in trivial or purely practical tasks that erode capacity for elevated thought and literary creation; preserve mental space for higher work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh others' thoughts; be open to modifying views
rubrics_metrics.description: Be 'disposed to weigh the thoughts of other thinkers' and 'ready to modify his views by consideration of theirs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise intellectual humility: critically engage with predecessors and peers, allow their arguments to inform and alter your positions when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject rigid traditionalism that suppresses individual judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid doctrines of 'practical infallibility' (e.g., unquestioning consentient teaching) that 'involves the depreciation of authority' of individual reason in theological or intellectual matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept canonical or traditional statements uncritically; preserve role of individual intelligence and judgment when addressing doctrinal or philosophical claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let literary study enable independent formation of belief
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature 'has no other bearing on a man's religious opinions than as it leaves him more at liberty to form them for himself than any other.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broad literary inquiry to foster autonomous thinking rather than to reinforce received dogma; encourage self-formation through reading and reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a balance between contemplative freedom and steady routine
rubrics_metrics.description: A lack of regular profession can 'disease' the mind by unsteadiness, while a regular calling 'tends to steady the mind' and restrain distracting tentations of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek a balance: some structured work or routine can stabilize judgment and purpose, but avoid allowing routine to wholly suppress contemplative freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid partisan alignment; resist making doctrine a party vehicle
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not make party the vehicle of doctrine; parties and party-organizations can divert and corrupt thought—party spirit often departs from truth and wastes talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write with universality and moral seriousness rather than servicing sectarian, partisan, or factional agendas; beware of treating ideas primarily as instruments of party promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be historically and philosophically informed about sources
rubrics_metrics.description: When appealing to early writers (e.g., the Fathers), recognize that some were materialists and that forms of doctrine may rest on obsolete metaphysics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not uncritically rely on historical authorities whose underlying philosophy contradicts current understanding; contextualize historical claims and test them by sound metaphysical and historical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reducing spiritual or abstract doctrines to crude material metaphors
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticizes the tendency to conceive the soul as composed of 'subtle matter' or to treat spiritual presence as a material indwelling; warns against 'insisting upon shadows as if they were realities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve conceptual clarity when discussing spiritual/metaphysical themes—use metaphor cautiously and avoid converting metaphor into literal doctrine that distorts moral and spiritual meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style must illuminate truth, not merely ornament it
rubrics_metrics.description: Critiques 'brass'—polished but hollow style—versus 'gold'—genuine, spiritually effective writing; warns that mere rhetorical gilding can obscure Scripture/truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor sincerity and substance in prose: stylistic polish should serve to reveal and support truth, not mask emptiness; avoid decorative language that substitutes for real insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray moral/spiritual transformation as cooperative, not wholly passive
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejects fallacy that people are wholly passive in spiritual re-creation (seed/ground metaphors); emphasizes co-operation and the role of the will and moral agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting character change or spiritual growth in writing, account for human agency and co-operation with formative influences rather than presenting transformation as purely automatic or passive.
